title: "Linear Models in R"
subtitle: "Course 1 · the basic course"

## Audience and aims

Early-career PhD students in CBB (behaviour, cognition, neuroscience) with mixed statistical backgrounds. After the course, they can formulate, fit, check, interpret and report linear models in R on their own data, and they know when to seek advice.

## One framework, not a toolbox of tests

Everything is a linear model; t-tests and ANOVA are shown as special cases. The final sessions each relax one assumption: normality (GLM), then independence (GLMM).

## Format

A **three-week block course with 11 sessions**. Each day combines

- a short **theory input**,
- **guided live coding**, and
- **supervised exercises** (with basic and advanced parts).

::: {.box}
**Before the course:** a mandatory [R primer](../resources.qmd#r-primer) sets a common baseline (R, RStudio, data import, the tidyverse basics, plotting, Quarto).
:::

## Materials

Quarto slides, R scripts and exercises for every session are linked on the session pages. All code runs on the datasets in the [`data/`](https://github.com/SimonStephan31/cbbstats/tree/main/data) folder of this site's repository.

## Assessment

- **Exercises** during the course.
- A **final project**: in the last days, students analyse a dataset (their own or one provided) and present it briefly. This links the course directly to individual [consultation](../consultation.qmd). See [Final project](final-project.qmd).

## Software

Please install before the course:

- a current version of [R](https://cran.r-project.org/) and [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/)
- [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) (bundled with recent RStudio versions)
- the course packages:

```r
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "lme4", "glmmTMB", "emmeans",
                   "performance", "DHARMa", "car"))
```
